question: If the amount at the end of the 2nd year and 3rd year on a certain principal at compound interest is ₹12,000 and ₹13,200 respectively, find the rate of interest per annum.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In compound interest, the amount from the previous year becomes the principal for the next year.

Interest for the 3rd year = Amount of 3rd year − Amount of 2nd year

⇒ Interest = 13200 − 12000 = ₹1200

Rate of Interest (R) = Interest ÷ Principal of that year

⇒ R = 1200 ÷ 12000 = 0.1

**∴ The correct answer is 0.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 Rate = R

**Given:**

Amount at the end of the 2nd year (A₂) = ₹12,000

Amount at the end of the 3rd year (A₃) = ₹13,200

**Formula Used:**

Amount for n years, A = P(1 + R)ⁿ

**Calculations:**

⇒ For 2 years: P(1 + R)² = 12000 --- (Equation 1)

⇒ For 3 years: P(1 + R)³ = 13200 --- (Equation 2)

⇒ Dividing Equation 2 by Equation 1:

⇒ [P(1 + R)³] ÷ [P(1 + R)²] = 13200 ÷ 12000

⇒ 1 + R = 1.1

⇒ R = 1.1 − 1

⇒ R = 0.1

**∴ The correct answer is 0.1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest Formula

The amount after n years is given by A = P(1 + R)ⁿ, where P is the principal and R is the decimal rate of interest.

Simple vs Compound Interest

For the first year, both Simple Interest (SI) and Compound Interest (CI) are equal if compounded annually on a given principal.

Successive Amounts in CI

The ratio of amounts for any two consecutive years is always constant and equal to the multiplying factor (1 + R).
